summary: Structurally valid. The run-to-file mapping, the QC/phospho split, both overrides of Experimental_Design.xlsx (activation method per run; K4R6/K8R10 for incorporation runs A1-A16) and the ontology terms were all independently confirmed. One important finding: all 36 RW3 rows (incorporation digests and mix check 1) claim a Lys-C digestion that the protocol places only after the first trypsin-only digest, i.e. only for the RW5 (digest-of-digest) runs.

reviewer_context.context: fresh isolated subagent with no producer transcript; producer manifest and validation log treated as untrusted; primary evidence re-fetched into scratchpad/PXD038505/review-qc-1

spec_compliance.evidence: 56 rows x 37 columns; templates ms-proteomics v1.1.0 + vertebrates v1.1.0 + clinical-metadata v1.0.0, all released versions in templates.yaml. clinical-metadata says it applies to any organism and licenses characteristics[genotype]. vertebrates is not mutually exclusive with clinical-metadata. Reserved words are spelled correctly, modification syntax is valid (Acetyl uses PP=Protein N-term), and the repeated cleavage-agent, modification and template columns are legal. sdrf-tools structure OK.

ontology_integrity.evidence: OLS4 resolved every term with the right label and none is obsolete: NCBITaxon:10090, UBERON:0000956, CL:0010012, MONDO:0100039 'CDKL5 disorder', PATO:0000461, PATO:0000384, EFO:0005857 'mouse embryo stage', EFO:0022397 C57BL/6, MS:1001742, MS:1000083, MS:1000133, MS:1001251, MS:1001309, PRIDE:0000627, UNIMOD:481/188/259/267. sdrf-tools check: 18/18 verified, no UNIMOD swaps.

source_evidence.evidence: Re-fetched Experimental_Design.xlsx, IncorporationandConversionCalculations.xlsx, mqpar.xml and DNU7717QCtxt.zip from the PRIDE FTP; range-read the headers of all 36 QC raw files plus the RW8/RW9/RW10 files of A17. Override 1 holds: the RW8 header reads 'TiO2 C1 CID' / Top10CID.meth, RW9 'MSA' / Top10MSA.meth and RW10 'HCD' / Top10HCD.meth, so the design sheet is wrong; all 36 QC runs are Top10CID 70 min on an LTQ Orbitrap Velos. Override 2 holds: the Incorporation summary.txt puts Labels1 = Arg6;Lys4 on A1-A8 and Arg10;Lys8 on A9-A16, and the per-experiment peptide counts tie A1 to medium 2.1 (3058) and A9 to heavy 2.1 (3277). Genotype per channel for E1-E6 matches the design sheet and the paper ('3x heavy WT/light KO and 3x heavy KO/light WT'). Failing point: Lys-C on the RW3 rows (see findings).

file_mapping.evidence: PRIDE v3 files/all (projectAccessions=['PXD038505']) lists 66 .raw files. The QC SDRF holds 36 and the phospho SDRF 30; the two sets do not overlap and together equal the deposited set exactly. All are vendor .raw files. A13RW3 is not a blank: its header reads 'Digest of LB-13' and the search found 4118 peptides.

design_consistency.evidence: Rows: 16 single-label incorporation runs + 10 mix check 1 runs x 2 + 10 mix check 2 runs x 2 = 56. No collisions on (source, biological replicate, technical replicate, fraction) or on (source, assay, label). Each culture dish is its own source. Controls C1-C4 mix the same culture in both channels. Controls 3 and 4 have no incorporation run, so their technical replicates run 1-2. The split is justified: the QC SDRF holds unenriched digests and the phospho SDRF holds TiO2-enriched runs.

omission_safety.evidence: Lys-C is asserted for runs digested with trypsin only (important finding). All other values trace to cited sources, and Control characteristics are left 'not available'.

deterministic_validation.evidence: flock ... parse_sdrf validate-sdrf -s <artifact> -t ms-proteomics -t vertebrates -t clinical-metadata: exit 0, with one warning (C57BL/6 is not in NCBITaxon). sdrf-tools check exit 0 (CLEAN). sdrf-tools score 94/100. sdrf-tools structure exit 0.

findings.location: comment[cleavage agent details] (2nd column, NT=Lys-C;AC=MS:1001309) on all 36 rows whose data file ends RW3 (A1-A16 RW3 incorporation; A17-A26 RW3 mix check 1)
findings.message: Lys-C is claimed for runs taken before any Lys-C step. Only the RW5 runs (A17-A26 RW5, 'Digest of Digest of ...') follow the second digestion, which used Lys-C and then trypsin.
findings.evidence: PMC10713615 Methods: 'o/n digestion trypsin ... desalted ... before further digestion ... using Lys-C for 2 hrs, followed by o/n trypsin digestion ... Mixing and digestion checks were performed after each digestion step.' Raw sample names: RW3 = 'Digest of E1/C1', RW5 = 'Digest of Digest of E1/C1', A1-A16 = 'Digest of LB-n' (single digest). Correction: on the RW3 rows, set the Lys-C column to 'not applicable' (ms-proteomics 1.1.0 sets allow_not_applicable: true for cleavage agent details) and keep Trypsin; keep Trypsin + Lys-C on the 20 RW5 rows; update the manifest claim to match.

findings.location: comment[label] SILAC light on K4R6 rows
findings.message: K4R6 is labelled 'SILAC light' although it carries isotopes. The producer documented the choice and the authors' design sheet uses it, but the deposited calc sheet and the QC search call it 'medium', and some converters (DIA-NN constants) read 'light' as mass 0. Consider 'SILAC medium'; many repository K4R6/K8R10 SDRFs use medium + heavy.
findings.evidence: IncorporationandConversionCalculations.xlsx 'Ratio H/L medium 2.1'; sdrf_pipelines converters/diann/constants.py SILAC light masses [0,0]

findings.message: The recommended column is missing. It is not stated in the QC parameters.txt for MaxQuant 1.3.0.5.

The request asks for neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's. CDKL5 deficiency disorder is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, not a neurodegenerative disease. The user should confirm the dataset is in scope before contribution.
findings.evidence: Paper abstract: 'CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD, DEE2), one of the most common genetic epilepsies'
